Objective-only evidence supports testing multiple negatives before changing SASRec’s architecture. [gSASRec (IJCAI 2024 extended abstract; original RecSys 2023)](https://ijcai.org/proceedings/2024/939) combines increased negative counts with generalized BCE to reduce sampling-induced overconfidence. This addresses calibration and training stability, not false-negative identification. [A Theoretical Analysis of Recommendation Loss Functions under Negative Sampling (2025)](https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/abstract/document/11228603) finds categorical cross-entropy and BPR equivalent with one negative; conclusions favoring full-catalog cross-entropy do not automatically transfer to sampled training. Compare multi-negative BCE, gBCE, and sampled softmax under matched compute.

For adaptive hardness, [R²NS (WWW 2026)](https://renzhaochun.github.io/assets/pdf/WWW_2026_Camera_Ready.pdf) uses uniform-negative warm-up, efficient approximate global recall, and curriculum re-ranking. It reports that introducing hard negatives too early can underperform uniform sampling. Random selection among several high-scoring candidates mitigates false-negative risk; highest score alone does not establish a true negative. A cheaper experimental adaptation would warm up uniformly, then gradually mix uniform negatives with randomly selected top-ranked candidates from a modest pool, excluding observed training interactions. This adaptation remains a hypothesis for the benchmark.

[SoftmaxLoss@K (KDD 2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.05673) uses quantile-based truncation and a smooth NDCG@K surrogate, reporting efficient optimization and noise robustness. Its NDCG motivation does not guarantee sampled HR@10 gains. Prioritize controlled loss-only trials, then sampling-only trials; compare negative counts, hardness schedules, and elapsed GPU time. Select exclusively through unchanged four-category macro validation HR@10; the Industrial_and_Scientific wrong-rank diagnostic motivates investigation but cannot establish improvement.
